purpose: integrity and resource check run BEFORE the full sweep, as required by the task

software.note: torch and transformers versions are IDENTICAL to those recorded in the archived layer-8 extraction metadata

pilot.throughput_vs_layer8_only_run: 2.81 vs 4.11 seq/s; pooling 33 layers instead of 1 costs ~1.46x

layer8_agreement_with_archived_embedding.cause: the archived run transferred residue-level activations to CPU and pooled there in float32; this run pools ON DEVICE in float32 before transfer, and the length-sorted batch composition differs. Both effects change float16 reduction order.
layer8_agreement_with_archived_embedding.decision: DO NOT reuse the archived layer-8 embeddings. Numerical provenance differs, so the frozen protocol's reuse condition (input, model, pooling AND numerical provenance must match) is not met. All 33 layers come from ONE self-consistent extraction instead, so every layer in the sweep is comparable to every other.

disk_constraint.float32_verdict: would leave ~0.15 GB free; rejected as unsafe
disk_constraint.decision: store pooled vectors as float16; COMPUTE the pooled mean in float32 on device, then cast

measured_effect_of_float16_storage.layer_independence: the per-layer minimum cosine spans only 0.999999642-0.999999881, i.e. the storage effect is uniform across layers and cannot reorder them
measured_effect_of_float16_storage.comparison: this is the same order of magnitude as the pooling-device difference already present between this run and the archived one

memory_pressure_observed.note: the host was under heavy swap pressure during the run (disk ~99% full, so swap could not grow). The extraction proceeded correctly but with the process frequently in uninterruptible wait. Recorded because it affects wall-clock timings reported here, not results.
